name: Polarized optical microscopy of a crystallization / phase transition from 203 K to 393 K
plain_name: Watch a crystal melt or change phase under a polarizing microscope
description: Watch crystallization and melting of a synthetic wax under a polarized optical microscope while the temperature is scanned between 203 K and 393 K on a liquid-nitrogen-cooled hot-cold stage.

sources.citation: Design of Crystal Growth Dimensionality in Synthetic Wax: The Kinetics of Nonisothermal Crystallization Processes
Investigating the Crystallization Kinetics and Mechanical Properties of Poly(Butylene Succinate): The Dual Role of Polyoxymethylene Blending and MWCNT Heterogeneous Nucleation

reported_conditions.as_printed: Linkam THMS600 with liquid nitrogen pump
DSC companion runs 1-30 K/min (POM ramp rates not stated)
second procedure: sample between two glass slides

requirements.rationale: The wax procedure scanned 203-393 K; this is the paper's range and the user should confirm it for their sample.
Observation through a polarized optical microscope needs optical access to the sample.
Optional: the second (PBS) procedure heated at 30 °C/min; the wax paper does not state POM ramp rates.

Condensation/frost: a cold specimen or window below the frost point collects ice unless the sample space is evacuated or purged with dry gas (pm_015, pm_016). Applies only when the operating temperature is at or below 0 °C.

params.name: operating_temperature
params.description: Lowest temperature of the scan (203 K)

missing_information: POM heating/cooling rates of the wax procedure
controlled slow cooling (<= 10 K/min) is needed to observe the Cr1 phase (DSC observation, ex2_A_009); a stage's ability to hold a slow controlled rate is not modelled
confirmation_note: Profile author reviewed the requirements on 2026-10-31; users must re-confirm edited values.
